Neither solution is correct. The equation gives $|x-4| = 12$, so $x - 4 = 12$ or $x - 4 = -12$, which yields $x = 16$ or $x = -8$. The product is $16 \times (-8) = -128$.

Solution A sets up the wrong equation. It treats $x-4$ as $2$ or $-12$ instead of solving $|x-4| = 12$, so both roots ($6$ and $-8$) are wrong except that $-8$ happens to be correct. Its product, $-48$, is wrong.

Solution B sets up the cases correctly. The first case, $x - 4 = 12$, gives the correct root $x = 16$. In the second case, $-(x-4) = 12$ gives $x - 4 = -12$, but B wrote $x - 4 = -8$, an arithmetic slip, so it got $x = -4$ instead of $-8$. Its product, $-64$, is wrong.

Both final answers are wrong, but B's method is sound and its error is a single arithmetic slip, so it is marginally closer to a correct solution.

WINNER: B
